{{c|{{larger|TO TIMOTHEE.}}}}

{{dropinitial|T}}HE cheefe {{ls}}cope of this {{ls}}econd to Timothee, is, to open vnto him that his martyrdom is at hand. Which yet he doth not plainely before the end: preparing fir{{ls}}t his minde with much circum{{ls}}tance, becau{{ls}}e he knew it would grieve him {{ls}}ore, and al{{ls}}o might be a tentation vnto him. Therfore he talketh of the cau{{ls}}e of his trouble, & of the reward: that the one is honorable, and the other mo{{ls}}t glorious: and exhorteth him to be con{{ls}}tant in the faith, to be ready alwaies to {{ls}}uffer for it, to fulfil his mini{{ls}}terie to the end, as him{{ls}}elf now had done his.

Whereby it is certaine, that it was written at Rome, in his la{{ls}}t apprehen{{ls}}ion and empri{{ls}}onment there: as he {{ls}}ignifieth by the{{ls}}e wordes Cap. 1: ''One{{ls}}iphorus was not a{{ls}}hamed of my chaine, but when he was come to Rome, carefully {{ls}}ought me, &c.''
